A double battle, at sea and on land, fought in 469 or 466 BCE at the mouth of the Eurymedon River in Pamphylia, southern Anatolia. The fleet of the Delian League under the Athenian general Cimon beat the forces of the Persian Empire under Xerxes I.

Persia had gathered a fleet and army on the south coast, likely for a new push into the Aegean. Cimon, son of Miltiades the victor of Marathon, attacked first. He destroyed or took the Persian fleet, landed his men, and beat the Persian army on the shore the same day. He then caught Phoenician reinforcements before they arrived.

The win ended the Persian threat to the Aegean for a generation and made Cimon the leading man in Athens. It also changed the league: with Persia beaten back, Athens kept collecting tribute and turned its allies into subjects. Fighting with Persia went on until the disputed Peace of Callias around 449 BCE.
